Tweet 1:
S3 just became a self-describing data lake. Annotations let you attach rich, mutable, queryable metadata directly to objects — no more syncing external databases that drift over time.

Tweet 2:
1/ The old problem: raw data in S3, context somewhere else. Clinical trials, regulatory docs, lab results — all dependent on metadata in separate systems that constantly fall out of sync.

Tweet 3:
2/ What S3 Annotations actually enable:
• 1000 annotations per object, up to 1GB structured metadata
• Mutable without rewriting the file
• Queryable via Athena, Redshift, or any Iceberg engine
• Native discovery layer for AI agents

Tweet 4:
3/ For AI workflows, this matters. Agents can now discover datasets, retrieve summaries and embeddings, understand lineage and QC status — all without downloading the object. Context-aware data discovery, built into S3.

Tweet 5:
S3 Annotations remove entire classes of infrastructure for regulated industries. If you're building AI pipelines on life sciences data, this changes the architecture.
